 J U D G M E N T

The Police Inspector, Vyalikaval police station, Bengaluru has submitted charge sheet against the accused persons for the offences punishable U/s.498-A, 306, 114 r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code in Vyalikaval PS., Crime No.220/2013.
2.

The brief story of the prosecution are as under:

sentences.text: The deceased-Smt.Hemavathi (Roopa) is the daughter of the complainant.
The deceased-Smt.Hemavathi (Roopa) and Somashekarachar are the wife and husband.
The marriage of deceased and accused was performed on 29.08.2009.

After marriage, the deceased and accused were residing together at No.6, 6th cross,
Nagappa road, P.G.Halli, within the limits of Vyalikaval PS.

At that time, the accused Nos.1 to 4 have been harassing the deceased and her child mentally without providing any basic needs and abetted her to die and on 01.06.2013 accused No.1 with the instigation of accused Nos.2 to 4 informed deceased that he will look after the child and she has to leave the place, again on 05.11.2013 accused No.1 with the instigation of accused Nos.2 to 4 refused her and told that he is not interested to live with her and left the place with the clothes, due to which deceased Hemavathi @
Roopa @ Hemalatha wrote Death Note and between 3.00 and 6.00 p.m. deceased committed suicide by hanging herself to the ceiling fan with a veil and towel at her matrimonial home and thereby the accused have committed the offences alleged against them.
3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the jurisdictional VIII ACMM.,
Bengaluru.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C, by furnishing charge sheet copies to the accused persons.
The same was numbered as SC No.600/2014.
4. The accused Nos.3 and 4 were discharged on 07.03.2015.
Hence, charge was framed against the accused Nos.1 and 2 only for the offences punishable U/s.498-A, 306 and 114 r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code.
The accused Nos.1 and 2 have pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
Later the accused No.2 died as per the death certificate.
Hence, the case against accused No.2 was abated and case against accused Nos.3 and 4 were discharged.
5. The prosecution has examined twelve witnesses as PW.1 to 12 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P32 and MOs.1 to 5.
On behalf of accused, Ex.D.1 got marked.

On consent of accused counsel,
inquest Mahazar, postmortem report have been marked at EX.P4 and P11.
The learned PP has given up C.Ws.18, 19, 20, 23 and 24.
The court has issued SS and proclamation against the witnesses CWs.3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 15, 16, 17, 18.
Inspite of sufficient time granted, the concerned police failed to keep present the said witnesses before court.
As such the prayer of learned PP was rejected and the witnesses CWs.3, 6, 7, 9, 15, 16, 17 and 18 were dropped and thereby the prosecution side evidence was taken as closed.
6. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused No.1 as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused No.1 has denied incriminating evidence present against him, and not opted to lead defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.

The accused No.1 has complied Sec.437-A of Cr.P.C.
7. Heard the arguments of both sides and perused the materials on record.

8. The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
Vyalikaval P S vs Somashekarachar on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45337875/
2

sentences.text: 1. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 being the husband of deceased- Smt.Hemavathi @ Roopa @ Hemalatha subjected deceased mental harassment for silly reasons and not providing basic needs and thereby the accused No.1 has committed the offence punishable under Section 498-A of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proves that due to the the accused No.1 giving harassment for silly reasons to deceased, the said deceased was mentally tortured and attempted to commit suicide for two times and due to torture deceased gave complaint to Halasuru Gate Women Police and Vanitha Sahayavani, later accused No.1 was giving torture, due to which on 05.11.2013 when accused No.1 left the house with his clothes, due to which deceased wrote death note and between 3.00 to 6.00 p.m she hanged herself to the ceiling fan with veil and towel and thereby committed the offence punishable under Section 306 of IPC?
3. What order?
9.This Court findings on the above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: As per final order  for the following:-
 R E A S O N S 10.
Points No.1 and 2 : These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.
Admittedly, the deceased and accused No.1 are the wife and husband.
Due to the marital relationship, the deceased has given birth to a male child.
The both accused and deceased along with their child residing at No.6, 6 th cross, Nagappa road, P.G.Halli.

At that time, the accused Nos.1 to 4 have been harassing the deceased and her child mentally without providing any materials and abetted her to die and on 01.06.2013 accused No.1 with the instigation of accused Nos.2 to 4 informed deceased that he will look after the child and she has to leave the place, again on 05.11.2013 accused No.1 with the instigation of accused Nos.2 to 4 refused her and told that he is not interested to live with her and left the place with the clothes, due to which deceased Hemavathi @
Roopa @ Hemalatha wrote Death Note and at 3.00 to 6.00 p.m. deceased committed suicide by hanging herself to the ceiling fan with a veil and towel at her matrimonial home and thereby the accused have committed the offences alleged against them.
11.
The prosecution is required to establish the physical and mental harassment having received by the deceased from the accused.
To prove the said allegations, the prosecution has examined PW1-Susheelamma who is none other than the mother of the deceased.

The said witness PW1 is being signatory to the complaint has not supported the contents of the complaint though the Vyalikaval P S vs Somashekarachar on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45337875/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
3 complaint allegation shows that the accused has been harassing the deceased soon before her death,
but the evidence given before the court by the said witness does not establish any mental torture given by the accused No.1 to the deceased to commit suicide.

Similarly, the witnesses PWs.2, 4 to 6 are being the relatives have not spoken anything with regard to mental harassment given by the accused No.1 and due to which deceased ended her life by hanging herself.
No doubt the said witnesses have given proper evidence with regard to the marriage of accused and deceased.
But the said witnesses have denied giving of mental harassment by the accused to the deceased.
The complainant PW1 has also not supported the Mahazar and statement alleged to be given before the police.

Since, the evidence of PW1, 2, 4, 5, 6 goes against to the root of the prosecution case, hence,
the learned PP has cross- examined the said witnesses.
But unfortunately not able to get any useful evidence in support of prosecution.
12. Such being the case, the prosecution has examined PW1-Susheelama and PW3-S.Nagaraj who are also the signatories to the Inquest mahazar marked at EXP4, to prove its contents.

The said pancha witnesses did not supported conducting of Inquest Mahazar marked at EX.P4 by deposing that the police have not conducted mahazar in their presence and they do not know the contents of the mahazar.
As such, learned PP has treated the panchas i.e., PW1 and 3 as hostile with the permission of court and cross-examined.
The learned PP has failed to elicit any useful evidence to believe due to the mental harassment given by the accused, the deceased has ended her life.

Hence,
the evidence of the mother of the deceased, brother- in-law of deceased and panchas not worthful to the case of prosecution to establish guilt against the accused.

13. The prosecution has examined PW4-Nanjundachar, P.W.5 Krishnachari, P.W.6 Harisha being the relatives of a accused No.1, P.W.7 Bettaswamy, owner of the house in which accused No.1 and deceased were living on rental basis and P.W.8 Sharada wife of P.W.7.
The said witnesses PWs.4 to 8 have completely turned hostile.
As such, learned PP has treated them as hostile with the permission of court and cross-examined.
Even in the cross examination, they have failed to support the case of the prosecution.
The learned PP has failed to elicit any useful evidence to believe due to the mental harassment given by the accused, the deceased has ended her life.

Hence, the evidence of the relatives and owner of accused not worthful to the case of prosecution to establish guilt against the accused No.1.
14.

The evidence of PW9-Smt.A.S.T.Shyamala Devi retired PSI shows that on 01.06.2013 the deceased Roopa @ Hemalatha came to police station and gave complaint, she received the complaint and registered NCR.350/2013, on 08.06.2013 she called the accused No.1 and deceased and advised them.
Later for further conciliation/advise, she informed to appear before Vanitha Sahayavani.

The evidence of PW10-Smt.Saraswathi Senior Councillor shows that on 21.01.2014 she gave the complaint handed over by the deceased to Vanitha Sahayavani.
15.

The evidence of PW11-Smt.K.M.Manorama, being Executive Magistrate shows that on 06.11.2013 Vayalikaval police station have given request letter to conduct Inquest Mahazar, on the same day between 1.30 to 2.30 p.m she visited the Mortuary of Bowring Hospital and before the panchas CWs.6 to 8 conducted Inquest Mahazar as per Ex.P.4 and recorded statements of CWs.1 to 4 and 9 and handed over deceased dead body to doctor for post mortem.
Vyalikaval P S vs Somashekarachar on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45337875/
4 16.

The evidence of PW12-K.Shankarachar, Retired PI, shows that on 05.11.2013 at 7.30 p.m he received phone call from accused No.1 that his wife Roopa has committed suicide by hanging herself by locking the door, which is located at No.6, 6th cross, P.G.Halli, Bengaluru.

Immediately, he went alongwith police staff and found that deceased has committed suicide by hanging and the accused was not present at that time, they informed the same to C.W.3, later C.W.3 came alongwith her husband to the police station.
On 06.11.2013 at 12.15 a.m C.W.1 came to the police station and lodged complaint.
He received the complaint and registered FIR.220/2013.

As the deceased died within 3 years of her marriage, hence informed to Tahasildar and sent the body to Victoria hospital for post mortem, and thereafter conducted spot panchanama and seized death note and also prepared rough sketch and the death note marked at Ex.P.23 and the pages are at Ex.D.1 and 2.
Later collected marriage invitation card and two photos taken at the time of marriage.

The panchanama was marked at Ex.P.24, photos at Ex.P.25, invitation card at Ex.P.26, 100 page books at Ex.P. 27 and 28, 3 photos at Ex.P.29 and photo containing plastic paint box at Ex.P.30 and recorded statement of CW.2, C.W.5, C.W.13 and C.W.14 as per Exs.P.1, P.3, P.8 and P.9 respectively.
The FSL Report is marked at Ex.P.31 and after completion of investigation has submitted charge sheet against the accused.
The learned accused counsel has completely denied the evidence given by the police official witnesses PW9 to 12.
It is no doubt, the prosecution has got marked inquest report at EX.P4 and postmortem report at EX.P11 on consent of accused counsel.
The postmortem report issued by the medical officer shows that the death is due to asphyxia as a result of hanging.
It is no doubt the death of deceased-Smt.Hemavathi (Roopa) is due to hanging.
The death note marked not support the case of the prosecution.
Whether the said death was due to the harassment of the accused No.1 as alleged against him is not proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt.
So it is very clear that the prosecution has failed to establish that the accused has harassed the deceased mentally and due to which, the deceased has committed suicide.

Hence, in view of above reasons,
this court has answered point No.1 and 2 in the Negative.
17. Point No.3:

In view of answer of court on points No.1 and 2, this court pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable U/s.498A and 306 of Indian Penal Code .
The bail and surety bond of accused No.1 stands cancelled.
MO1 to 5 being worthless shall be destroyed after appeal period is over.
